```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```


```{r}
library(nososim)
devtools::load_all()
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Define a landscape

`make_landscape()` gives one row per location, with a `capacity` column.

```{r}
hospital <- list(
  Geneva = list(
    ICU = c(a = 2, b = 3),
    General = c(a = 1, b = 4, c = 2)
  ),
  Gallen = list(
    ICU = c(a = 3, b = 5),
    General = c(a = 2, b = 4, c = 1)
  )
)
landscape <- make_landscape(hospital)
```

## Define admissions and individuals

The `admissions()` function returns a vector of counts, one per row of `landscape`. It receives a daily copy of the landscape with an `available` column containing the number of free spaces. It returns actual admissions, which must not exceed availability. 

```{r}
landscape <- landscape |>
  mutate(
    filling_prob = case_when(
      level_1 == "Geneva" & level_2 == "ICU" ~ 0.9,
      level_1 == "Geneva" & level_2 == "General" ~ 0.7,
      level_1 == "Gallen" & level_2 == "ICU" ~ 0.8,
      level_1 == "Gallen" & level_2 == "General" ~ 0.5
    )
  )

admissions <- function(landscape, date) {
  rbinom(
    nrow(landscape),
    size = landscape$available,
    prob = landscape$filling_prob
  )
}
```


The `individuals()` function returns a table of admitted people, one row per person, with attributes and stay dates. `individuals()` must return `admitted` with, at least, the following additional columns:
- start: a Date equal to `date`.
- end: a finite Date on or after `start`, including this last day.
Any additional columns are optional—for example, id, age, or role.

```{r}
individuals <- function(admitted, date) {
  admitted |>
    mutate(
      id = paste0(format(date, "%Y%m%d"), "_", row_number()),
      age = sample(18:90, n(), replace = TRUE),
      role = "patient",
      los = case_when(
        level_2 == "ICU" ~ sample(3:7, n(), replace = TRUE),
        level_2 == "General" ~ sample(5:10, n(), replace = TRUE)
      ),
      start = date,
      end = start + los - 1L #-1 for inclusive end date
    )
}
```



## Generate a population

`make_population()` returns a table of admitted people, one row per person, with attributes and stay dates. It calls your `admissions()` and `individuals()` functions for each day in the date range. Capacity becomes available on the day after `end`.

```{r}
dates <- seq(as.Date("2024-01-01"), as.Date("2024-01-30"), by = "day")

set.seed(123)
population <- make_population(
  landscape,
  dates,
  admissions = admissions,
  individuals = individuals
)

population |>
  select(id, starts_with("level_"), age, role, start, end) |>
  head(10)
```

## Plot stays

Each plot row represents one unit of capacity, grouped by location. Stays run
from `start` through `end` (inclusive); grey lines show unused capacity.

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
autoplot(population, aes(colour = id)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Extract daily contacts

`get_contacts()` returns a matrix of contacts between people present on a given date. Each row and column represents one person, and the value is 1 if they share a set of attributes on that date, 0 otherwise. Use `by` to choose which columns must match.

```{r}
get_contacts(population, dates[1], by = c("level_1", "level_2", "role"))
```

For a matrix on each date:

```{r}
contacts <- lapply(dates, function(date) get_contacts(population, date))
names(contacts) <- as.character(dates)
```
